title: The Masked Marvel

evidence.note: UNVERIFIED renewal. In the raw text of this volume, the Name Index lists 'THE MASKED MARVEL. (R)' under both 'Repix, Inc.' and 'Republic Productions, Inc.' (at about character 557,484 of 911,227 in the archive.org full-text file). The '(R)' marks a renewal. The full renewal entry was not seen in the raw text, so the renewal registration number, renewal date, original registration number and claimant wording are unconfirmed, and no page number is confirmed. Coverage of this check: about 96% of the full-text file (characters 0 to 875,597); the last ~35,000 characters were not read. To confirm, open the volume linked here, go to the Renewal Registrations section, and look for 'MASKED MARVEL'.

editorial:
The Masked Marvel is a 12-chapter Republic Pictures serial released on 6 November 1943. A masked hero in a business suit fights the Japanese saboteur Sakima and his espionage organization. The audience is not told who the hero is until the final reel; he is one of a group of four special investigators. Chapter 1 is titled 'The Masked Crusader'. Source for the summary and chapter title: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Masked_Marvel

The trap is a renewal that appears to be recorded but is unverified. The Name Index of a 1971 Catalog of Copyright Entries volume lists 'THE MASKED MARVEL. (R)' under Repix, Inc. and Republic Productions, Inc. The full renewal entry was not seen, so its number, date and page are unconfirmed. The print and score layers are therefore marked undetermined, not public domain. Do not treat this serial as a public-domain source. Clearing it would need a licence from the rights holder or a legal determination from counsel. The title and character names may also carry separate franchise or trademark claims, which this dossier did not check.
faq: Is The Masked Marvel (1943) public domain?

Can I use clips from the Internet Archive copy?

Not safely without a licence. Hosting on the Internet Archive does not change copyright status. If the renewal is confirmed, it would likely cover the photoplay, including its soundtrack. Clips would need permission from the current rights holder, or a fair-use analysis for your specific use.
